policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV text reads anarthrous "a feast of the Jews", and the mapped textual_variant note ("Many ancient authorities read the feast") explicitly consigns the articular reading to the margin. The base without the article is what the ASV rendered.
The variant is only the article before the personal name Iesous; English "Jesus went up" is identical either way and the chapter's one note here concerns the feast, not this article.
ASV text transliterates "Bethesda", and the mapped textual_variant note places Bethsaida and Bethzatha among "some ancient authorities" in the margin. The text form matches the base spelling.
ASV reads "a multitude of them that were sick" with no quantifier; the added polu would give "a great multitude", which the ASV does not render and does not italicize.

ASV text ends the verse at "withered"; the mapped textual_variant note reports the waiting-for-the-moving-of-the-water plus angel material only as what "many ancient authorities insert". The shorter base reading is in the text.

"thirty and eight years" is the ASV's ordinary compound-numeral idiom (cf. its "threescore and ten" style), so the English "and" does not testify to a kai between the numerals. Both readings yield the same wording.
ASV reads "in his infirmity" with "his" unitalicized, i.e. rendered rather than supplied; that possessive answers to autou, which the alternative omits.

Egeire and Egeirai are alternative imperative forms of one verb with one sense; the ASV's "Arise" renders either. The verse's only note is an alternative_rendering about "pallet" and cannot decide a reading.
ASV renders the connective: "It is the sabbath, and it is not lawful for thee". The omitting reading leaves the two clauses asyndetic, which the English does not reflect.

ASV reads "to take up thy bed" with "thy" unitalicized, so the possessive is rendered from sou rather than supplied; only r02 carries sou. The two base spellings (krabatton/krabbaton) are indistinguishable in English, so the possessive is the deciding element.
ASV opens "But he answered them", so the adversative de is rendered and the omitting reading (r02) is excluded. Between hos de and ho de the English "he" is identical, so those two remain open.

ASV begins the verse asyndetically, "They asked him", with no rendering of oun; the ASV renders oun in this very chapter ("So the Jews said", 5:10; "Jesus therefore answered", 5:19), so its absence here reflects the shorter text.
ASV quotes the command in full: "Take up thy bed, and walk?" The base reading has only Aron; the object phrase ton krabatton sou is present in the English and unitalicized.
The variant is only the order of the enclitic pronoun and ti; "lest a worse thing befall thee" renders either arrangement identically.
ASV reads "went away, and told the Jews that", an announcing verb with a direct personal object; the ASV renders eipen as "said" throughout this chapter (5:8, 5:19), so "told" answers to anengeilen.
ASV has only "the Jews persecuted Jesus, because he did these things on the sabbath"; the longer reading's added clause "and sought to kill him" is nowhere in the ASV verse.
ASV names the subject: "But Jesus answered them". The base reading has only the pronoun with de, which would give "But he answered them"; "Jesus" is unitalicized and so rendered from the text.
ASV's "answered and said unto them" fits both the imperfect elegen and the aorist eipen; the ASV regularly renders elegen with a simple "said", so the English does not distinguish the tenses here.
ean and an are interchangeable in the indefinite relative clause; "for what things soever he doeth" renders either without difference.

The variant is only the future's active versus middle inflection of one verb; "shall hear" renders both. The verse's note ("Or, hearken") is an alternative_rendering about English wording and decides nothing.
zesousin and zesontai are active and middle futures of the same verb with the same sense; ASV "shall live" renders either.
The readings differ only in the position of edoken relative to kai to huio; "even so gave he to the Son also" is compatible with both orders.

The added kai is an adjunct particle that need not surface in English; ASV "and he gave him authority to execute judgment" already opens with "and" and reads naturally on either text, so the wording does not distinguish them.
Active and middle future forms of the same verb; ASV "shall hear his voice" renders both alike.
ASV renders the connective between the two clauses: "and they that have done evil". The omitting reading leaves the second member asyndetic; the ASV's "and" reflects de.
ASV reads "the will of him that sent me"; the longer reading would give "the Father that sent me", and no "Father" appears in this ASV verse.
meizo and meizon are alternative forms of the same comparative; "is greater" renders either.

ASV uses the English perfect, "the works which the Father hath given me to accomplish", answering to the perfect dedoken; the aorist edoken would be the ASV's "gave" (as it renders edoken in 5:26 of this same chapter).

The added ego is an emphatic subject pronoun already carried by the verb ending; ASV's "the very works that I do" supplies "I" from the verb and its "very" renders auta, so the English does not show whether ego stood in the text.
ekeinos and autos in this intensive position both come out as the ASV's resumptive "he hath borne witness of me"; the English does not separate them.
The readings differ only in whether popote precedes or follows the verb; ASV "Ye have neither heard his voice at any time" fits either order.
Word order only, the participle before or after the prepositional phrase; ASV "his word abiding in you" renders both.
